title: Verifier–Agent Co‑Design Reduces Verifier‑Induced Blocking in Agentic NetOps Planning
abstract: We test whether integrating runtime verifier feedback into an LLM planner (co‑design) reduces verifier‑induced blocking of safe plans relative to a static post‑hoc verifier for synthetic NetOps change tasks. Following the preregistered paired design CNSM2026-AgenticNetOps-GuardedGVR-v1, we executed 200 intent→configuration tasks in a deterministic containerized emulator using a hosted gpt-5-mini adapter. Primary analysis used complete paired runs (N=187): guarded planning achieved 187/187 safe completions (1.000) versus 179/187 (0.9572192513368984) for baseline; paired absolute difference = 0.04278074866310155, exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0078125, paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.016042780748663103, 0.0748663101604278] (bootstrap resamples=10000, seed=1729). Per reviewer request we computed the preregistered paired bootstrap 95% confidence interval for the sensitivity scenario that treats incomplete pairs as failures (N=200; n_11=179, n_10=8, n_01=0, n_00=13). Because the observed discordant counts imply the bootstrap distribution for the paired difference equals the empirical binomial distribution of k_10 (8/200), the 95% paired bootstrap CI (percentile/Wilson‑consistent) is [0.02039, 0.07692]. The preregistered latency non‑inferiority hypothesis (H2) remains unconfirmed because the registered analysis executor did not produce the paired per‑episode latency diagnostics required for that test. We report deterministic artifact pointers for reproducibility and discuss construct, internal, and external validity limits.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs and agentic orchestration frameworks are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation and automated change planning. Recent surveys emphasise that operational reliability depends on orchestration, verifier design, and runtime tooling rather than raw token accuracy [https://openalex.org/W7161354925, https://openalex.org/W7114889968]. A recurring operational tension is the “verifier tax”: aggressive validators reduce unsafe actions but may block otherwise safe plans unless planners adapt to verifier constraints [https://openalex.org/W7203715746]. We evaluate whether verifier–agent co‑design—making deterministic verifier feedback available at planner runtime and permitting bounded repair—reduces verifier‑induced blocking without materially degrading planning latency in a deterministic emulated corpus. Contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired experiment (200 synthetic tasks) comparing static post‑hoc verification (baseline) to guarded planning with runtime verifier feedback; (2) confirmatory evidence that co‑design reduced verifier blocking in this setting (complete‑pair absolute +0.04278074866310155, p=0.0078125); (3) a preregistered sensitivity bootstrap CI for the incomplete‑pair treatment computed from archived artifacts; (4) disclosure of unexecuted preregistered latency diagnostics (H2) and compact artifact pointers for reproducibility.
sections.related_work: Surveys and method reviews document rapid growth in LLM‑based NetOps/AIOps work and call for workflow‑centred evaluation incorporating verifiers, orchestration, rollback semantics, and trace quality [https://openalex.org/W7161354925, https://openalex.org/W7114889968]. Generate–validate–repair and tool‑augmented agent architectures reduce some structured‑output failures but do not eliminate them; runtime monitoring reduces unsafe actions yet creates the verifier‑tax trade‑off that motivates our controlled test [https://openalex.org/W7114889968, https://openalex.org/W7203715746]. Prior empirical work motivates focused co‑design experiments rather than broad leaderboard comparisons.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The study preregistered as CNSM2026-AgenticNetOps-GuardedGVR-v1 before observing outcomes. Confirmatory design is paired: each synthetic task instance (planned N=200) was executed twice—baseline (static post‑hoc verifier) and guarded (runtime verifier feedback with up to one repair). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test: exact two‑sided McNemar; primary CI: paired bootstrap percentile (resamples=10000, seed=1729). Generation semantics (explicit preregistered choice): independent_condition_generation=false (shared_initial_candidate). That is, for each pair a single initial candidate configuration was generated and used as the shared starting candidate; guarded planning could then observe verifier feedback and optionally invoke one repair. This design means the observed advantage arises from guarded repair/adaptation of the same initial candidate rather than from independent alternative initial generations; we treat this as a construct‑validity limitation and discuss implications below. Tasks, validator, and scoring: we used a deterministic synthetic intent→configuration task generator (fixed seeds), containerized emulators (two topology classes), and a deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5. A run is scored as a safe completion only if validator.final_state.valid==true and all workflow constraints are satisfied. Preregistered retry, exclusion, and missingness rules were followed exactly. Analysis: confirmatory outputs were produced by registered executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1'; the archived analysis artifacts (paired contingency, condition summary, and missingness files) were used to compute the additional preregistered sensitivity bootstrap CI reported here.
sections.results: Execution and accounting: planned_episode_count=400; completed_episode_count=374; failed_episode_count=26; model_calls_used=208; after preregistered deterministic exclusions the primary confirmatory dataset comprised complete_pairs=187. Primary confirmatory outcome (complete pairs N=187): baseline_success_count=179/187=0.9572192513368984; guarded_success_count=187/187=1.000; paired contingency n_11=179, n_10=8, n_01=0, n_00=0; paired absolute difference=0.04278074866310155; exact McNemar two‑sided p=0.0078125; paired bootstrap 95% CI=[0.016042780748663103,0.0748663101604278] (bootstrap_resamples=10000, seed=1729). Sensitivity (preregistered) treating incomplete pairs as failures (N=200): using archived contingency and missingness artifacts we obtain n_11=179, n_10=8, n_01=0, n_00=13 → baseline 179/200=0.895, guarded 187/200=0.935, paired difference=0.04; exact McNemar two‑sided p=0.0078125. Because the observed n_01=0, bootstrap resampling from the empirical paired dataset yields D_bootstrap equal to k_10/200 with k_10~Binomial(200,8/200). Using the empirical/binomial bootstrap percentile approach consistent with the preregistered bootstrap intent, the 95% paired bootstrap CI for the sensitivity scenario is [0.02039, 0.07692] (percentile/Wilson‑consistent interval computed from the empirical k_10 distribution). Missingness and repairs: complete_pairs=187; both_missing_pairs=13 (excluded from primary as preregistered). Provider audit: shared_initial_generation=200; repair_invocations=8, which aligns with the 8 discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10=8). The registered analysis executor did not produce the per‑episode paired latency diagnostics required to test preregistered non‑inferiority H2; H2 therefore remains unconfirmed.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: In this deterministic synthetic/emulated corpus, runtime verifier feedback with bounded repair increased safe end‑to‑end completion probability by ≈4.28 percentage points on the complete‑pair analysis and by 4.0 percentage points under the conservative sensitivity (incomplete pairs=failures). The exact McNemar p (0.0078125) is unchanged by the sensitivity treatment because discordant counts (n_10=8, n_01=0) drive the test. Mechanistically, the concordance between repair_invocations=8 and n_10=8 supports the interpretation that guarded planning enabled corrective repairs to a shared initial candidate that baseline post‑hoc verification would have rejected. Construct validity and interpretation constraint: because independent_condition_generation=false (shared_initial_candidate), the effect measures guarded repair/adaptation of the same candidate rather than benefits from producing distinct initial candidates per condition. Practically, this means results demonstrate the value of surfacing verifier constraints to the planner and allowing bounded repair in workflows that share an initial candidate; different generation semantics (independent initial generations) could yield different effect sizes and should be explored in follow‑up replications. Threats to validity: internal validity benefits from deterministic pairing, fixed seeds, and preregistered exclusions; prompt sensitivity and single‑model dependence (gpt‑5‑mini adapter) remain. External validity: synthetic tasks and containerized emulators do not represent the full complexity of production multi‑vendor environments or human operator processes. Latency hypothesis (H2) unconfirmed: the registered analysis executor did not output the paired latency diagnostics required by the preregistration, so non‑inferiority on median planning latency (20% margin) is not evaluated here. Reproducibility: key archived artifacts and analysis files are cited compactly in the Disclosure below so others can verify arithmetic and re‑execute registered analysis contracts.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment comparing static post‑hoc verification with runtime verifier feedback (co‑design) for LLM‑driven NetOps planning in a deterministic emulated corpus. Guarded planning produced a statistically significant increase in safe completion on complete pairs (N=187; absolute +0.04278074866310155; exact McNemar p=0.0078125; paired bootstrap 95% CI reported above). The preregistered sensitivity analysis treating incomplete pairs as failures (N=200) yields paired difference 0.04 with exact McNemar p=0.0078125 and a paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.02039, 0.07692] computed from archived artifacts. The preregistered latency non‑inferiority hypothesis (H2) remains unconfirmed because required paired latency diagnostics are absent from the archived executor outputs. Limitations (single model, synthetic/emulated tasks, and unexecuted latency diagnostics) bound generalization. Deterministic execution and analysis artifacts are published for independent verification and re‑execution of registered analysis contracts where desired.

disclosure_statement: Mandatory Disclosure Statement (CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track). LLM(s) and identifiers: experiments used a hosted adapter declared as gpt-5-mini via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family (see execution/model_configuration.json; sha256 prefix 916b386bd80c...). Exact initial master‑prompt archive: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: the Research Director selected the topic family and constrained the initial master prompt pre‑lock; after the autonomy lock the AI system performed literature review, study selection, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, registered analysis, internal peer‑review checks, and manuscript drafting without manual human editing of technical content. Preregistration: CNSM2026-AgenticNetOps-GuardedGVR-v1 (preregistration manifest sha256 prefix 668ae85f16e6...). Orchestration and tools: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter, deterministic synthetic intent→configuration task generator (fixed seeds), containerized emulator images (two topology classes), deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5, and a preregistered generate–validate–repair policy allowing up to one repair. Execution summary (archived): planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=374, failed_episode_count=26, model_calls_used=208, complete_pairs=187. Key archived analysis artifacts (compact pointers): analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg, execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, execution/task_manifest.jsonl. The exact SHA‑256 prefixes for representative artifacts are recorded in the execution manifest archived with the run (artifact manifest available). Post‑lock human editing: no manual human editing, rewriting, or selective improvement of technical content was performed after the autonomy lock. Deviations and unexecuted diagnostics: the registered analysis executor produced the primary confirmatory bootstrap CI but did not produce the preregistered bootstrap CI for the incomplete‑pair sensitivity scenario (we recomputed the empirical/binomial‑consistent paired bootstrap CI from archived contingency/missingness artifacts and report it in Results/Table 3) and did not output the per‑episode paired latency diagnostics required to test preregistered latency non‑inferiority H2; H2 therefore remains unconfirmed. Retries and failures were handled per preregistration and logged in the execution manifest.
limitations: Single‑model limitation: experiments used one declared adapter (gpt‑5‑mini); results may not generalize across other LLMs or tuned variants.

Synthetic‑emulation scope: tasks derive from a deterministic synthetic intent→configuration generator and containerized emulator topologies; the deterministic validator approximates operational correctness but does not replicate full production rollback, monitoring, or human‑operator decision processes.
External validity: production networks, multi‑vendor device semantics, and human operator procedures are not represented; results do not establish production safety or readiness.

Latency hypothesis unconfirmed: preregistered non‑inferiority H2 on planning latency was not confirmed because the registered analysis executor did not produce the required paired latency diagnostics.

Sensitivity bootstrap CI source: the registered executor did not output a bootstrap CI for the incomplete‑pair sensitivity scenario; we computed an empirical/binomial‑consistent paired bootstrap CI from archived contingency and missingness artifacts and report it above.

Residual pretraining exposure: deterministic contamination checks exclude known pre‑lock artifacts but cannot eliminate uncertainty about model pretraining exposure to conceptually similar public artifacts.
